paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: : The performance on Llama3.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—on a task related to long-tail biomedical knowledge, as measured by accuracy (ACC) in percentage, across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is presented on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, with tick marks at 10¹ and 10². The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", represents the accuracy and ranges from 60% to 80%, with major gridlines at 60%, 65%, 70%, 75%, and 80%. The "Base" method (black line with circular markers) shows a steady increase in accuracy from approximately 61% to 67%. The "MEND" method (brown line with diamond markers) starts at about 66% and rises to approximately 74%. The "FT" method (blue line with triangle markers) begins at around 63% and increases to roughly 68%. The "MEMIT" method (purple line with pentagon markers) starts at approximately 66% and climbs to about 73%. The "ROME" method (green line with square markers) demonstrates the highest performance, beginning at approximately 72% and increasing to about 77%. Overall, all methods show an upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently outperforming the other methods across the entire range.
